::: {#def-evidence-lower-bound}
#### Evidence lower bound (ELBO)

Let $x$ be observed data,
and let $z$ be an unobserved [discrete random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv),
with [joint probability mass function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-joint-pmf) $\pf{x, z}$.
Let $q$ be a [probability mass function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pmf) for $z$.
Require that $q$ gives [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) zero
to every value $z$ where the [posterior](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/bayesian-inference.html#def-posterior) $\pf{z \mid x}$ is zero.
The **evidence lower bound** (**ELBO**) of $q$ is the average, over $z$ drawn from $q$,
of the difference between the [logarithm](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-logarithm) of $\pf{x, z}$
and the logarithm of $q(z)$:

$$\mathrm{ELBO}(q) = \sum_z q(z) \paren{\logf{\pf{x, z}} - \logf{q(z)}}.$$

The sum runs over the values $z$ with $q(z) > 0$.

:::
